name: Cowlitz River (below Mayfield Dam)
blurb: Big, dam-fed, easy river famous for salmon and steelhead — a fast, mellow float.

sections.notes: Busy fishing river — expect drift boats and anglers. Cold, powerful water. Both launches are run by Tacoma Power, which says there is no fee to use them (Blue Creek allows camping up to 3 days, no fires).
sections.mapPendingReason: Blue Creek (Cowlitz Trout Hatchery): Batch 1 (2026-10-25). Legal access is confirmed: Tacoma Power's Cowlitz Trout Hatchery page says Blue Creek Boat Launch (273 Blue Creek Lane, Toledo) gives free public river access, with 3-day camping in the lot. It gives an address only. No agency coordinate exists: WDFW's Facilities GIS has no ramp here, and its Blue Creek parking feature comment says it 'does not account for Tacoma Power's boat launch and assoc facilities'. The WDFW Blue Creek page is the ADA fishing-platform site. Imagery shows a ramp to the shore south of the lot near 46.4838, -122.7311, and boatlaunchmap/OSM give 46.48381, -122.73049, but neither is an agency source, and OSM maps a second unnamed ramp about 400 m upstream. Bank is river-right on NHDPlus HR (flow ~250), not usable until the point is verified. Imagery pass (2026-10-25, not promoted): Disputed site. Imagery (research/raw/batch4/bc19_g.png, z19): a paved lane from the trailer lot reaches the water (~46.48381,-122.73049, matching OSM), but OSM also maps a second ramp ~400 m upstream and no agency source says which one is Tacoma Power's. Not placed.

mapAuditNote: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 1). Tacoma Power confirms both launches (Barrier Dam, Blue Creek) are public and free, but it publishes addresses only. WDFW's Barrier Dam ramp feature sits at the ramp head in the lot, about 30-35 m from the water. Blue Creek has no agency ramp feature. Pending until on-ramp agency coordinates are found for both.
